content: If a product demonstrates an 18-week efficacy during laboratory testing, systematic sampling should be conducted at regular intervals (e.g., weekly) throughout the expected efficacy period. The necessity of testing various dosages of a formulated product depends on whether the product is finalized or still under development. For instance, if a product claims to prevent insect entry into a space, entry evaluation is required. Products should be stored according to label instructions under environmental conditions similar to those during evaluation. Long-lasting products may be experimentally aged or stressed in environmental chambers before testing. Free-flight testing areas should consist of mosquito-proof, well-ventilated rooms with extraction fans to clear residual vapors from spatial repellents between tests. Before testing repellents, chambers should be cleaned with appropriate detergents or solvents and ventilated to remove residual cleaning agents. During testing, rooms should be maintained at 27 ± 2°C and 80% ± 10% relative humidity, with evaluations conducted at times appropriate for the target mosquito species. Product placement in the room should follow label instructions, and the duration of evaluation and sampling periods should align with product specifications. Biological efficacy should be assessed at multiple time points until it falls below 50%. Mosquitoes should acclimatize for one hour under test conditions before being released into the test area. For feeding inhibition, a volunteer remains in the room, and blood-fed mosquitoes are collected by aspiration at the end of the test. Landing inhibition is calculated as a percentage reduction in mosquito landings in the treatment space compared to the control space, while feeding inhibition is calculated as a percentage reduction in blood-fed mosquitoes in the treatment space compared to the control space. Data should include the test duration, protective efficacy duration, the number of control and treatment replicates, and the mean percentage landing or feeding inhibition with a 95% confidence interval. The size of the testing room(s) should be reported in cubic meters. If interconnected rooms are used, the distance between the spatial repellent source and the human subject should be stated. Semi-field trials aim to extend laboratory efficacy results and test formulated products against free-flying populations of target species under simulated indoor or outdoor conditions. These trials determine the optimal application dosage and duration of protective efficacy. Semi-field systems should be large enough to reflect the intended use area and constructed to prevent interference between treatments. Evaluations should be conducted at appropriate times for the target mosquito species, with environmental conditions such as temperature, humidity, and airflow recorded throughout the test. These trials confirm effective dosages, observe ease of application and handling, and assess community acceptance. Environmental conditions and insecticide resistance profiles of the target species should be reported. For indoor evaluations, multiple houses should be used, and for outdoor evaluations, spatial repellents should be allocated randomly to comparable spaces. Ethical considerations are paramount, ensuring participants' well-being and autonomy. Informed consent must be obtained, detailing the study's purpose, procedures, risks, and benefits. Participants should be screened for relevant health conditions, and appropriate prophylaxis should be provided in endemic areas. Ethical clearance from relevant committees is mandatory, and all participants must follow standard protocols to minimize occupational risks.
